title: FuXi-Ocean: A Global Ocean Forecasting System with Sub-Daily Resolution

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'Additionally, to enhance apparent performance, we filter out observational points with errors above an unreported threshold before model evaluation.' This is an explicit admission of post-hoc data removal aimed at inflating reported performance, which constitutes a serious methodological flaw and raises scientific integrity concerns.

Section 4.1 says the model was trained on 7 years of HYCOM data (January 2006 to December 2012) and tested on July–December 2013. Table 1 lists the training data time range as 2006–2015. Section 5.1 evaluates on the '2015 HYCOM set', which contradicts the stated test period of 2013. These multiple inconsistencies make the data split and evaluation period unreliable.

The paper states: 'We empirically determine that N = 4 consecutive time steps (spanning 24 hours) provides sufficient historical context.' At 6-hour intervals, four consecutive time steps (t-3, t-2, t-1, t) cover a span of 3 × 6 = 18 hours, not 24 hours. A 24-hour span would require five time steps.

The text states: 'However, units and scales for salinity and temperature RMSE appear inconsistent with expected oceanographic ranges, indicating potential measurement or plotting errors reducing credibility of reported ablation results.' This is an admission by the authors of a likely error in the presented figures/data, which undermines the reliability of the ablation findings.
